label: <DEL> step of short (L=4-6) sequences starting with i (also j/h)
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.0065% of steps). 93% of activation mass is at the delimiter step (recall_idx 0), almost entirely for L=4-6 (t=4-6); it never fires in the copy phase and only weakly at a few late original-phase steps. It is strongly tied to the first original token (the token about to be output): i carries ~60% of mass (31x lift), j and h ~10% each, 0 and v a little. Magnitude is further raised by the last original token being p or 3 (prev_tok lift 13x / 9x) and by the second token being e or c (next_out lift ~10x); the top activations are all of the form i e c ... p/3 <DEL>. The predicate captures ~77% of mass but precision is only ~1%: most delimiter steps of short i-initial sequences do not activate it, and adding the p/3 and e/c cues raises precision only to ~10-20% while losing most recall. So the feature looks like a sparse conjunction of soft cues (first token i/j/h, short length, last token p/3, second token e/c) rather than one crisp condition. Does not fire on copy-phase steps, on L=3, or meaningfully on L>=7.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=i (+4.65), prev_tok=p (+4.19), orig2=c (+3.17), orig1=e (+3.03), orig0=h (+2.53), orig0=j (+2.44). Lower it: phase=2 (-2.30), in_first=0 (-2.02), t=8 (-2.01), in_count=1 (-1.45).
